title: ActionAuthorization
description: Permission for one exact operation, against one exact base, once. It is deliberately not the same object as approving a Product Contract (what should be built) or approving a Release (what may be published): conflating those is how approving a plan quietly becomes permission to do anything the plan touches. This is the generalisation of ApprovedBuildPlan, which held the same guarantees for one operation while every other mutating route enforced none of them.

operation.description: The exact registered operation name. An authorization for `project.generate` is not an authorization for `project.assets.replace`.

base.description: What this authorization was granted against. A base that has moved is a different thing to act on, and permission does not travel with it.

files.description: Repository-relative rules the operation may write. `*` is permitted and is a deliberate, visible statement rather than an omission.

environment.description: Where the effect lands. An authorization for a workspace is never an authorization for production.

idempotencyKey.description: The caller's name for this attempt. A retry carrying the same key is the same attempt; a different key against a consumed authorization is a second attempt and is refused.

proposedBy.description: Who asked. Recorded so the approver can be checked against it: nothing approves its own request (principle 17).
